body.objective: Add a bidirectional publication-coverage audit to Science Forge so the programme can verify that every publication-relevant certified result is represented in at least one current paper claim, and every material paper claim is backed by current scoped evidence. The existing discover/query.py stale-papers command detects only cited certificates that changed after their TeX source; it does not identify important results that never entered a paper, paper claims without evidence edges, overview-only results without a technical manuscript, superseded evidence, or lifecycle and claim-boundary disagreement. The first consumer is this pure-Weyl programme, whose mined graph currently contains 896 certificate nodes but only 38 unique certificates reached by the current TeX-cites edge model; that raw disparity is not itself a defect because most fixtures are supporting evidence, so the feature must include an explicit materiality policy.
body.stop_condition: Land an s-f paper-coverage command and deterministic gate over the evidence graph with: (1) a versioned annotation for result publication relevance/materiality, at minimum HEADLINE, TECHNICAL, SUPPORTING, NEGATIVE_RESULT, and INTERNAL_FIXTURE, with an explicit human-review queue for unclassified results; (2) typed result-to-paper edges distinguishing primary theorem, supporting evidence, limitation/open gate, negative result, supersession, and overview-only mention; (3) forward checks for every HEADLINE/TECHNICAL/NEGATIVE_RESULT result having at least one non-stale technical-paper disposition or an explicit DEFERRED/NO_PAPER_NEEDED rationale; (4) reverse checks for every material paper claim having a current certificate or explicitly typed literature/interpretive basis, declared lifecycle and dependency boundary; (5) detection of stale hashes or commit ordering, superseded certificates, contradictory lifecycle/boundary text, conflicting duplicate claims, and results mentioned only in Papers 00/98/99 but absent from a technical paper; (6) a human-readable matrix grouped by paper and by uncovered result plus machine-readable JSON; (7) advisory mode during active research and a fail-closed release/freeze mode; and (8) a deterministic fixture proving detection of an uncovered important negative result, an unsupported paper claim, a stale evidence edge, an overview-only result, and a correctly deferred internal fixture. Run the first advisory audit on physics/symplectic-reconstruction and report the highest-materiality gaps without treating the raw count of uncited certificates as a scientific verdict.
body.forbid: assuming every certificate deserves a paper; inferring scientific importance solely from filenames, text similarity, embeddings, citation count, or AI judgment; treating a prose mention as proof of theorem coverage; counting Papers 00, 98, or 99 as the sole technical home of a headline result; silently downgrading uncovered results; auto-editing papers, certificates, claim maps, or lifecycle states; accepting a paper citation whose target is superseded, hash-stale, or outside the paper's declared theory/background/phase-space/boundary scope; turning the advisory research audit into a per-commit blocker before the corpus has been classified.
notes: Existing partial capability: forge/tools/science-forge/discover/query.py stale-papers compares git commit times for mined TeX-to-certificate citation edges.

Existing project structure to reuse: explicit claim maps for Papers 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 91, plus the evidence graph's paper, tex_statement, certificate, atlas_entry, cites, evidences, and contains nodes/edges.
Desired release question: Are we leaving a material certified result only in a report, atlas row, or work-event stream, and is any published claim no longer supported by the exact evidence it names?
